You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with SOURCE, has the woman's jacket front moved toward being fully closed in EDITED, and is it fully closed with no visible opening along the closure?
node.criteria: Compare the same jacket-front closure region in SOURCE and EDITED. Assess whether the front panels have moved closer, and whether they meet continuously with no visible opening remaining. Distinguish the closure line from a flared outer panel. Account for changes in pose, occlusion, and visibility; if the relevant panels cannot be compared reliably, treat the observation as unresolved rather than inferring no progress or full closure.
node.binding: Compare the woman's jacket in SOURCE with that same jacket in EDITED, focusing on its actual front closure rather than the outer panel's silhouette. A turn or flare is not by itself evidence of closure progress or lack of progress; judge progress only where the corresponding closure region is visible enough to compare.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The corresponding closure region is reliably visible in both images and shows no movement of the front panels toward closure compared with SOURCE.
node.half_when: The corresponding closure region is reliably comparable and shows concrete but incomplete movement of the front panels toward closure, while a visible opening remains.
node.full_when: The jacket's front panels meet continuously along the closure, with no visible opening remaining; pose or occlusion does not conceal a potentially open part of the closure.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front closure is visible in SOURCE, with a dark opening between the panels. In EDITED, she has turned and the jacket is flared outward; the actual closure line is not reliably visible enough to establish that the panels moved toward meeting or that the jacket is closed. The flare alone is not closure progress, and the endpoint of continuous closure is not shown.

response.content: {"text":"The node already distinguishes the closure line from the flared outer panel and correctly treats an obscured comparison as unresolved. The trace’s evidence says the edited closure is not reliably visible, yet it assigns `fail`/zero progress; that conflates insufficient visibility with reliable evidence of no progress and conflicts with the rubric’s unresolved category. Refine the decision criterion so an obscured or pose-shifted closure yields unresolved, not no progress, and reserve zero for a reliably comparable closure showing no movement. Keep full closure contingent on the entire closure being visibly closed; do not infer it from the flare or from the reference label. This is a visual-evidence/criterion application issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
